name: Judeo-Arabic

ancestors.notes: Genetically the Judeo-Arabic varieties are regional Arabic dialects (spoken Judeo-Arabic tracks the local Arabic vernacular closely); Standard/Classical Arabic is kept as the macro-level genetic anchor, per the ar-x-maghrebi.json precedent.
Hebrew (and Aramaic) adstrate: shared liturgical/literary register, Hebrew-script orthography, and a Hebrew-Aramaic lexical stratum common across Judeo-Arabic varieties (Wikipedia: Judeo-Arabic).

notes: STUB / MACRO NODE. Judeo-Arabic (ISO 639-3 macrolanguage jrb) is the collective code for the range of Arabic varieties historically spoken and written by Jewish communities across the Arab world, traditionally in HEBREW SCRIPT (rather than Arabic script) and carrying a Hebrew/Aramaic lexical and liturgical adstrate. As a macrolanguage code it is a sociolinguistic/orthographic collective, not a single genetic node: each individual variety (aju Judeo-Moroccan, ajt Judeo-Tunisian, yhd Judeo-Iraqi, and others such as Judeo-Egyptian, Judeo-Yemeni, Judeo-Tripolitanian Arabic) is genetically just the local regional Arabic dialect with a Hebrew-script/Hebrew-adstrate literary tradition overlaid. This node exists so those varieties (aju.json, ajt.json, yhd.json) have a macro-level parent to resolve to, per the graph-connectivity rule; it carries no phonology of its own (graphemes/allophones empty) because there is no single Judeo-Arabic phonology to state — each individual language's own spec is the level at which sourced grapheme mappings belong.
